page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM64-based server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors with Neoverse-V3 cores. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core, and is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9gd.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving high scores in multi-threaded stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Its memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, reaching 729.18 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database and caching performance are notable, with Redis SET operations exceeding 506 million operations per second and Passmark database operations ranking in the top tier. However, single-core CPU performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% of tested systems.

This instance is highly efficient for large-scale, parallelized workloads that benefit from high core density and local NVMe storage without requiring GPU acceleration. The combination of 192 dedicated ARMv9 cores and 11.4 TB of local SSD storage makes it suitable for high-throughput database hosting, large-scale Redis deployments, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. The ARM64 architecture offers a favorable performance-per-watt and resource density profile, making it a cost-effective choice for enterprise-scale general-purpose and storage-heavy workloads.
